'''Yamuna Krishnan''' (born May 25, 1974) is a professor at the Department of Chemistry, [[University of Chicago]], where she has worked since August 2014. She was earlier a [[Reader (academic rank)|Reader]] in [[National Centre for Biological Sciences]], [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]], [[Bangalore]], [[India]]. Krishnan won the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]] for science and technology, the highest science award in India in the year 2013 in the [[chemical science|Chemical Science]] category.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dr. Samir K. Bramhachari Announces Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Award 2013 |url=http://pib.nic.in/newsite/erelease.aspx?relid=99698 |access-date=30 December 2013 |publisher=Press Information Bureau, Government of India}}</ref> In 2024, she was named the Louis Block Professor of Chemistry and the college.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Yamuna Krishnan {{!}} Department of Chemistry {{!}} The University of Chicago |url=https://chemistry.uchicago.edu/faculty/yamuna-krishnan |access-date=2025-11-17 |website=chemistry.uchicago.edu |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-07-02 |title=Yamuna Krishnan named Louis Block Professor of Chemistry and the College {{!}} Department of Chemistry {{!}} The University of Chicago |url=https://live-ucchem.pantheonsite.io/news/yamuna-krishnan-named-louis-block-professor-of-chemistry-and-the-college |access-date=2025-11-17 |website=live-ucchem.pantheonsite.io |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Krishnan was born to P.T. Krishnan and Mini in [[Parappanangadi]], in the [[Malappuram]] district of [[Kerala]], India.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bhatt |first=Jay |title=LibGuides: Chemistry: Notable Chemists |url=https://libguides.library.drexel.edu/c.php?g=176832&p=9937770 |access-date=2025-11-17 |website=libguides.library.drexel.edu |language=en}}</ref> She grew up in [[Chennai]], India.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Yamuna Krishnan – Encounters top@DIPC Zientziarekin solasean! |url=https://dipc.ehu.eus/en/science-society/topa/krishnan_en.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251117191732/https://dipc.ehu.eus/en/science-society/topa/krishnan_en.pdf |archive-date=Nov 17, 2025 |archive-format=PDF |access-date=Nov 17, 2025 |website=Donostia International Physics Center}}</ref>  As a child, she met [[S. Krishnaswamy (biologist)|S. Krishnaswamy]], Vice Chancellor of [[Madurai Kamaraj University]], who fostered her interest in science.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Lilavati's daughters: the women scientists of India |date=2010 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |isbn=978-81-8465-005-1 |editor-last=Godbole |editor-first=Rohini |edition=2. printing |location=Bangalore |pages=166–169 |editor-last2=Ramaswamy |editor-first2=Ram}}</ref> From a young age, she conducted her own informal [[Citizen science|home expiriments]].<ref name=":1" />

Krishnan earned her Bachelor's in Chemistry from the [[University of Madras]], [[Women's Christian College, Chennai]], India in 1993.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Yamuna Krishnan – Professor {{!}} University of Chicago Department of Chemistry|url=https://chemistry.uchicago.edu/faculty/yamuna-krishnan-professor|access-date=2020-08-16|website=chemistry.uchicago.edu|language=en|archive-date=1 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200801084602/https://chemistry.uchicago.edu/faculty/yamuna-krishnan-professor|url-status=dead}}</ref> She secured a Master's of Science in [[chemical science|Chemical Science]]s in 1997 and a [[PhD]] in [[organic chemistry|Organic Chemistry]] in 2002, both from the [[Indian Institute of Science]], Bangalore.<ref name="CV">{{cite web|url=http://www.ncbs.res.in/sitefiles/YK-CV-13-1_2.pdf|title=Curriculum Vitae of Yamuna Krishnan|publisher=[[National Centre for Biological Sciences|NCBS]]|access-date=2 January 2014}}</ref> Krishnan worked as a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral research fellow]] and an [[1851 Research Fellowship|1851 Research Fellow]] from 2001 to 2004 at the Department of Chemistry at the [[University of Cambridge]], UK.

==Professional experience==
Krishnan was a [[Fellow]] 'E' at [[National Centre for Biological Sciences]] from 2005 to 2009, at the [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research|TIFR]] in Bangalore, India, and then tenured [[Reader (academic rank)|Reader]] 'F' from 2009 to 2013 at the National Centre for Biological Sciences, [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research|TIFR]], Bangalore, India. In 2013, she was promoted to Associate Professor 'G' at the National Centre for Biological Sciences, [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research|TIFR]], Bangalore, India and moved to [[University of Chicago]] as a professor of chemistry in August 2014.

== Research ==
Krishnan's current research interests are in the areas related to structure and dynamics of [[nucleic acid]]s, nucleic acid [[nanotechnology]], cellular and subcellular technologies.<ref name="CV" />
Her lab tries to understand the functions from [[DNA]] beyond that of its traditional role as genetic material. They develop versatile, chemical imaging technology using self-assembled DNA nanostructures to quantitatively image second messengers in real time, in living cells and genetic model organisms.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://chemistry.uchicago.edu/faculty/yamuna-krishnan|title=Yamuna Krishnan &#124; University of Chicago Department of Chemistry}}</ref>
